St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church 58 Golden Jubilee 1976 – 2026

Our Sunday School

Before 1992|Dn. Markose Mani

SGMOC Sunday School

Before being ordained as a deacon, K.M. Mani was active in various capacities at SGMOC. One of his most cherished roles was that of Sunday School teacher; he felt that passing on the values and traditions of the Indian Orthodox Church was paramount to its continuation in the United States.

During his tenure as head of the Sunday School program at SGMOC, he was dedicated to teaching children about the Bible, the importance of the rituals in the Qurbana, as well as the stories of believers who led exemplary lives following Christ’s example.

His experiences in helping establish an Orthodox church in Rourkela, Orissa (India) shaped his views on the importance of preserving the church’s history and making sure children are aware of the sacrifices of their elders.

1992–1996|Lee K. George

My Journey in Sunday School

My journey as a Sunday School teacher spanned about a decade. It began in the early 1990s as an advisor to the youth league and a teacher for the combined high school classes. At the time, we worshiped in a rented church at 38th and Chestnut, where limited space meant Sunday School classes were held during morning prayers before Holy Qurbana.

At the end of 1992, then-vicar Very Rev. K. Mathai Cor Episcopos asked me to serve as Headmaster, a role I held through 1996. I fondly remember bringing together churches across Philadelphia for a combined OVBS because the smaller churches did not have enough students to hold programs individually. This became an important part of Sunday School life in the Philadelphia area. Another meaningful change was transforming the annual caroling service from a nighttime event in which only men participated into one led by the Youth League and Sunday School, allowing everyone—boys and girls, men and women—to participate in this annual celebration of Christmas beginning in 1994. The move to the Torresdale Church significantly enhanced our Sunday School program, giving each grade its own classroom space.

I thank Almighty God for the opportunity to serve in this capacity and pray for the continued success of our Sunday School Mission.

1998–2013|Paul J. Maret

A Journey of Faith and Service

My journey as Sunday School Principal began in 1998, when our founding vicar, Very Rev. K. Mathai Cor Episcopos, entrusted me with the responsibility of leading our Sunday School. Accepting this role was not easy, as our first child, Josh, was only a few months old. During those early years at our church on Torresdale Avenue in Philadelphia, we faced several challenges, including limited space and a small number of dedicated Sunday School teachers.

Despite these challenges, we remained committed to providing our children with a strong spiritual foundation. We conducted general sessions alongside individual class lessons to ensure that our students received a well-rounded Sunday School education. I am especially grateful to our Sunday School teacher at the time, Mrs. Mercy Varkey, who took the lead in conducting the general sessions and provided invaluable support throughout this period.

Our students also began building a strong record of participation and achievement through centralized examinations and talent competitions. One of the major highlights of these early years was hosting the area-level Orthodox Vacation Bible School (OVBS) at our church. This program was successfully conducted under the leadership of Mr. Korah T. Mani, who served as the Philadelphia Area Sunday School Coordinator at the time.

St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church 59 Golden Jubilee 1976 – 2026

Our Sunday School

A Period of Transition and Perseverance

A particularly challenging period came during the construction of our permanent church building in Bensalem. Following the sale of our Torresdale Avenue property, our Sunday School moved to a temporary rented church facility in Philadelphia.

The limited space presented even greater challenges, making it difficult to accommodate our students and conduct classes comfortably each Sunday. However, with the dedication of our teachers, the cooperation of our parents, and the enthusiasm of our students, we continued our ministry without interruption.

Although the circumstances were difficult, we remained committed to our responsibilities and did our best to ensure that our children continued to learn the Word of God. This period taught us the importance of faith, patience, teamwork, and perseverance in serving our church community.

Growth and Achievements in Bensalem

A new chapter began when we finally moved into our present church building in Bensalem. With God's grace, our parish began to grow, welcoming new families and bringing a significant increase in Sunday School enrollment.

During this period, our founding vicar, Very Rev. K. Mathai Cor Episcopos, stepped down from his position, and Rev. Fr. Shibu Venad Mathai was appointed as our new vicar.

Under the guidance of Shibu Achen, our Sunday School continued to grow in both participation and achievement. With more space and an increasing number of dedicated teachers, we were able to provide our students with greater opportunities to develop their spiritual knowledge and talents. Our Sunday School became increasingly active in area-level and Northeast American Diocese-level programs and competitions.

One of the proudest moments in our history came in 2011, when our Sunday School won the Overall Championship in the Northeast American Diocese Sunday School Talent Competitions. This remarkable achievement reflected the dedication, hard work, and talents of our students and teachers. It was a memorable milestone for our parish and a testament to what we could accomplish through faith, commitment, and teamwork.

Reflections and Acknowledgments

In 2013, after fifteen years of service, I stepped down from my position as Sunday School Principal. Looking back on this journey as we celebrate our parish's Golden Jubilee, I feel deeply grateful for the opportunity God gave me to serve in this ministry.

We began with limited space and a small number of teachers, experienced the challenges of temporary facilities, and eventually witnessed the growth of our Sunday School in our beautiful church building in Bensalem. Through every stage, God's grace sustained us and helped us continue our mission of nurturing our children's faith.

I am sincerely thankful to Almighty God for His continued blessings, to our clergy for their spiritual guidance, to our teachers for their dedication and sacrifices, to our parents for their constant support, and to our students for their enthusiasm and commitment. It has been a blessing to witness the growth of our Sunday School and to see many of our former students grow into responsible adults and leaders in their own communities.

As we celebrate this important milestone in our parish's history, I pray that our Sunday School will continue to flourish and guide future generations in the knowledge and love of our Lord Jesus Christ.

May God bless our parish and grant us many more years of faithful service and spiritual growth. Submitted with prayers,

Paul J. Maret • Sunday School Principal (1998–2013)

St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church 60 Golden Jubilee 1976 – 2026

Our Sunday School

2013–2016|Sunitha Zacharia

Faith, Fun, and Fellowship

When Rev. Fr. Shibu Mathai invited me to serve as Principal of our Sunday School in August 2013, I accepted the opportunity with both gratitude and humility. Leading a ministry of more than 100 children was a tremendous responsibility, but it was also one of the greatest blessings of my life. I was privileged to work alongside devoted clergy, teachers, volunteers, parents, and students who shared a common mission—to help our children grow in their Orthodox faith and develop a personal relationship with our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ.

I was fortunate to follow faithful leaders who had already established a vibrant Sunday School ministry. Under the leadership of Paul Maret, with the guidance of advisors such as Mercy Varkey and Korah Mani, a strong foundation had been laid. My hope was simply to build upon their vision while introducing new opportunities for our children and families to learn, serve, and grow together.

Ministry is never the work of one person, and I was fortunate to have wonderful people serving alongside me. Our Registrar faithfully served alongside Reny Biju as Dean. When the Registrar later accepted diocesan responsibilities, Jimmy Varghese stepped into the role. Their dedication, encouragement, and friendship helped make those years both successful and deeply rewarding.

During my tenure, our guiding theme was Faith, Fun, and Fellowship. We wanted every child and family to experience a Sunday School that not only strengthened their faith but also created lasting friendships and joyful memories within the life of the Church.

Growing in Faith

Bible projects and presentations.

Our primary goal was always to help our children deepen their understanding of the Orthodox faith. We introduced general sessions focused on Christian virtues and values that encouraged spiritual growth beyond the classroom, published regular Sunday School newsletters to keep families informed, created a Sunday School bulletin board to celebrate student achievements and communicate important events. Beyond weekly classroom instruction, students created interactive Bible projects and displays illustrating Jesus’ journey to Calvary during Holy Week. These exhibits encouraged creativity, teamwork, and reflection while making learning engaging and memorable.

Living Our Faith Through Service

Faith was strengthened through service. Our Sunday School served meals to the homeless through Broad Street Ministry, sponsored a child from St. Thomas Ashram in Attappady, organized blanket drives, began participating in Operation Christmas Child, and visited Deer Meadows Nursing Home during Christmas to share the joy of Christ through caroling.

Christmas caroling at Deer Meadows Nursing Home.

St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church 61 Golden Jubilee 1976 – 2026

Our Sunday School

Building Fellowship

Sonday Funday — family fellowship.

Our theme, Faith, Fun, and Fellowship, came alive through Family Nights, apple picking, pumpkin carving, Ice Cream Socials, and especially Sonday Funday. These events strengthened friendships among children, parents, teachers, and volunteers while reinforcing that the Church is one family.

Looking Back with Gratitude

Looking back, I treasure not only the programs we introduced but the relationships that were formed. I remain deeply grateful to Rev. Fr. Shibu Mathai, our leadership team, teachers, volunteers, parents, and students. My prayer is that our efforts helped create a Sunday School where every child felt welcomed and experienced Faith, Fun, and Fellowship while growing closer to Christ.

“Train up a child in the way he should go...” — Proverbs 22:6

2016–2020|Reny Biju

Reflecting on SGMOC Sunday School

President: Rev. Fr. Shibu V. Mathai • Dean: Jessy Mathai (2016–19), Shainey Jacob (2019–20) • Registrar: James Varughese (2016–19), Jinu John (2019–20)

During this period, the Sunday School team continued to build on the well-established structure it inherited, while bringing new and innovative ideas that furthered its growth and vitality. With Rev. Fr. Shibu Mathai’s vision and guidance, and the steady leadership of Reny Biju, Jessy Mathai, James Varughese, Shainey Jacob and Jinu John, the Sunday School community grew not only in achievement but in its commitment to faith, service, and fellowship.

Strengthening the Foundation of Teaching and Learning

“Train up a child in the way he should go; even when he is old, he will not depart from it." Proverbs 22:6

This period saw a renewed focus on strong, structured teaching, supported by well-established guidelines for both the general session and individual classroom sessions. In support of this effort, the Sunday School conducted Teacher Enrichment Workshops and Fellowships, equipping teachers with valuable tools and techniques for the classroom. Experienced secular and religious educators led practical, hands-on sessions designed to make classroom teaching more engaging and effective. Blending substance with fun, the workshops were met with great appreciation and left a lasting impact — teachers came away better prepared, and in turn, children became more engaged in their learning.

A First for Our Youth

“Whether therefore ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God." 1 Corinthians 10:31

The Sunday School marked a historic milestone with its first-ever Nuhro Retreat, "The Orthodox Way of Life" (based on John 4:23), from August 18–20, 2017 at Sandy Cove Ministries in Maryland — our first offsite retreat experience, drawing 90 participants including parents, teachers, and children. The weekend featured teachings from Rev. Fr. Abey George, Rev. Fr. Alexander Kurien, Rev. Dn. Bobby Varghese, Rev. Dn. Saju Varghese, and Rev. Fr. Shibu Mathai, and combined worship (Evening and Morning Prayers, Confession, and Holy Liturgy) with themed workshops for separate

St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church 62 Golden Jubilee 1976 – 2026

Our Sunday School

parent, youth, and children's groups, plus outdoor activities like ziplining, swimming, fishing, and a riverside bonfire. A particular highlight was Evening Prayer held under a lakeside gazebo with a stunning sunset backdrop, whose beauty and serenity left everyone deeply inspired and spiritually uplifted. Offering students a time of fellowship, reflection, and spiritual renewal, the retreat set the tone for similar retreats going forward.

A New Sunday School Mission Team Takes Root

"As each has received a gift, use it to serve one another, as good stewards of God's varied grace." (1 Peter 4:10)

Mission and charity work at SGMOC Sunday School has always come from the heart — driven by volunteers eager to serve. As the program grew, so did the opportunity to bring even more structure and stewardship to that generosity. The impulse to serve was always there; the structure around it wasn't.

Recognizing an opportunity to build on that spirit, a dedicated Sunday School Mission Team was created. For the first time, all Sunday school mission and charity projects had a formal home — a team responsible for planning, coordinating, and being accountable for the resources entrusted to them. Mission Statement – “to serve through projects that involve and benefit children, staying rooted in the community we serve”

The team's first initiative, the Kerala Backpack Project, was launched in response to the catastrophic 2018 Kerala floods, which displaced millions and devastated communities across the state, including families connected to our own congregation. The Mission Team rallied to collect and distribute 300 backpacks filled with essential school materials for students whose education had been disrupted by the disaster — a powerful early expression of faith lived out through service. This act of service was appreciated by His Holiness Baselios Marthoma Paulose II, who sent a video message of appreciation.

Many other projects like Rise Against Hunger, Thanksgiving meals at local schools, Christmas Caroling and Crafts at a Nursing Home became annual activities. Recognizing that a child's growth extends beyond the classroom, the team conducted a variety of religious and wellness seminars aimed at supporting the spiritual and mental well-being of our children — reflecting a commitment to caring for the whole child: mind, body, and spirit.

What started as a Sunday School initiative didn't stay small. The groundwork laid by this team — the structure, the accountability, the focus — became the foundation for something bigger: the SGMOC Mission Board, now established at the parish level.

Gregorian Harmony: Voices Raised in Worship

“Serve the Lord with gladness: come before his presence with singing." – Psalms 100:2

Sunday School teachers came together to form Gregorian Harmony, a music team dedicated to praising the Lord through song. What began as a shared love for music among teachers soon grew into a ministry of its own — the team lent their voices to various parish and area-level events, filling each occasion with worship and joy.

Beyond the music itself, Gregorian Harmony became a space for fellowship — a place where teachers who serve the church in the classroom could come together and serve in a different way, through song. Their performances were not just presentations, but offerings — moments of praise that brought the community closer to God and to one another.

Gregorian Harmony stands as a reminder that ministry takes many forms, and that music, when offered in worship, has the power to unite and uplift a congregation.

Champions on the Stage

"Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights" (James 1:17).

The Philadelphia Area Talent Competition brings together Sunday Schools from across the region each year, giving

St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church 63 Golden Jubilee 1976 – 2026

Our Sunday School

students a platform to showcase their God-given gifts while building confidence and camaraderie with sister parishes. SGMOC's students turned in a remarkable performance, claiming the title of Area Champions in both 2018 and 2019 — a back-to-back achievement reflecting the depth of talent nurtured within our program. This achievement was a fruit of quiet faithfulness: teachers who prayed over their students, mentors and parents who saw and nurtured potential, and children who were taught that their gifts belonged first to God. Honors came in singing, storytelling, elocution, group song, and Bible Quiz. Rounding out this remarkable stretch, the Sunday School was proud to be Diocese Bible Quiz Champions in 2019, reflecting the students' deep engagement with Scripture. Looking back, what remains is the deeper truth: every gift discovered and every talent nurtured is a testimony of God's faithfulness — planted in these children, now growing into a lifelong offering of praise.

Faith in the Face of a Pandemic

When COVID-19 struck in 2020, the Sunday School immediately transitioned to remote, online teaching to keep the mission of learning and worship alive. Teachers and children alike embraced this new approach with resilience and openness. While the warmth of in-person interaction was sorely missed, the community's commitment to loving and learning God's word together never wavered, proving that faith could adapt and endure even in the most uncertain of times

2020–2025|Shainey Jacob

Sunday School — A Legacy of Faith, A Future of Promise

As St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church celebrates its Golden Jubilee, we give thanks to Almighty God for His abundant grace and guidance throughout these fifty blessed years. Sunday School is more than a classroom or a weekly gathering. It is a ministry of faith formation, where young minds are introduced to the richness of Orthodox Christian traditions, the teachings of our Holy Church, the Scriptures, the lives of the saints and the importance of living a Christ-centered life. Over the years, our Sunday School has been blessed with dedicated clergy, principals, teachers, parents and volunteers who have faithfully served this ministry.

Growing Together Through the Years

The history of our parish reflects God’s continued guidance and the collective efforts of its members. From the establishment of the parish in 1976, through the acquisition of our Bensalem property and the consecration of our church, each milestone represents a chapter of faith, perseverance and growth.

Challenges, Resilience and New Opportunities

Our Sunday School journey has also been one of growth, adaptation and perseverance. Even during the unprecedented challenges of the COVID-19 pandemic, our ministry remained committed to ensuring that faith education continued. It was at this time that I led the ministry as the Principal. Through the dedication of our teachers and the support of parents, we were able to sustain Sunday School classes and maintain a connection with our students during a time when gathering in person was not possible. This experience reminded us that faith formation is not confined to the walls of a classroom or church; it is a lifelong journey that continues within our homes and communities.

Investing in the Next Generation

Recognizing the changing needs of today's learners, our Sunday School ministry continues to embrace innovative teaching methodologies and curriculum development while remaining firmly grounded in the traditions, liturgy and teachings of the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church.

During my leadership in the ministry, we introduced Bloom’s Taxonomy as an educational framework that encouraged a

St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church 64 Golden Jubilee 1976 – 2026

Our Sunday School

more comprehensive approach to learning, moving beyond memorization and helping students understand, apply, analyze, evaluate and creatively engage with biblical teachings and Orthodox Christian traditions. Additionally, the introduction of the Talmido curriculum has provided new opportunities to enrich faith-based learning through structured lessons, engaging activities and age-appropriate resources.

These initiatives reflect our commitment to making Sunday School meaningful, interactive and relevant to the lives of today's children, while strengthening their understanding and appreciation of our Orthodox faith.

Faith, Fellowship and Action

Beyond classroom learning, our students have actively participated in various mission-oriented initiatives and Diocese-level activities, extending their faith into action through service, fellowship and Christian witness. Their involvement in workshops, Bible quizzes, talent shows, competitions and other Diocese-sponsored programs has provided valuable opportunities to discover and showcase their God-given talents. Through their enthusiasm, dedication and accomplishments, our students have earned numerous recognitions, accolades and words of appreciation, bringing pride to our parish. These experiences have reinforced the importance of teamwork, service, spiritual growth and representing our parish with faith and integrity.

"Train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old he will not depart from it." – Proverbs 22:6

As we celebrate fifty years of God's faithfulness to our parish, may we recommit ourselves to the sacred responsibility of nurturing the faith of our children. May the seeds of faith planted in our classrooms today grow into strong roots that sustain generations to come.

With hearts filled with gratitude, we celebrate the past, embrace the present and entrust the future of our Sunday School to God's loving care.

Glory be to God for all things!

Shainey Jacob • Sunday School Principal (2020–2025)

2025–2026|Dr. Sherin Kurian

Growing in Christ

Dean: Dr. Renny Thomas • Registrar: Dr. Ajeesh Cherian

Our Vision: Growing in Christ

With gratitude to God and excitement for the year ahead, we began our term in September 2025 for the 2025–2026 Sunday School year. Guided by our commitment to nurturing the spiritual growth of our children, we sought to create meaningful opportunities for students and families to deepen their faith, build lasting friendships, and strengthen our church community.

Our vision for 2025–2026 was:

Learn and grow in the FAITH, HOPE, and LOVE of Christ!

• Faith in Christ to Faith OF Christ

• Hope in Christ to Hope OF Christ

• Love in Christ to Love OF Christ

This vision reminded us that our mission extends beyond teaching our children about Christ. We strive to help them develop a personal and lasting relationship with Him, embodying His faith, hope, and love in their everyday lives.

St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church 65 Golden Jubilee 1976 – 2026

Our Sunday School

Our Sunday School ministry is blessed with approximately 100 students and 30 dedicated teachers who faithfully support this mission. Together, we are committed to creating an environment where children can grow spiritually, develop a deeper understanding of our Orthodox faith, and build a strong foundation for a lifelong walk with Christ.

Sunday School participation in diocesan ministry.

Activities and Fellowship: Building Memories Together

Candle-Making Class: Sharing God-Given Talents

Candle-making session.

One of our first activities was a candle-making class graciously led by our very own Elsa Abraham and her family. Our students enjoyed learning a new skill through this creative and engaging experience. What a beautiful example of sharing a God-given talent with others! We are grateful to Elsa and her family for generously giving their time and talents to make this activity memorable for our students.

Apple Picking: Harvesting Joy and Fellowship

We continued the year with a wonderful apple-picking outing that brought together our Sunday School students and their families. The event was well attended, and everyone enjoyed picking apples, sharing laughter, and savoring delicious apple cider. It was a wonderful opportunity for our families to connect outside the classroom and create lasting memories together.

Our First-Ever Sunday School Thanksgiving Dinner

Continuing our spirit of togetherness, we hosted our first-ever Sunday School Thanksgiving Dinner. The evening was filled with prayer, fun games, and joyful fellowship. It also provided a meaningful opportunity to pause and reflect on the many blessings in our lives. We were reminded of the importance of gratitude, faith, and the gift of belonging to a loving church community.

Thanksgiving fellowship.

Orthodox Vacation Bible School: United in Faith

Sunday School children in faith and fellowship.

One of the significant highlights of our ministry was hosting Orthodox Vacation Bible School (OVBS) at our church for the first time in many years. We were delighted to welcome children from both our parish and St. George Orthodox Church in Fairless Hills for this special spiritual experience.

St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church 66 Golden Jubilee 1976 – 2026

Our Sunday School

Our OVBS theme, “Be Mindful and Stay Blessed” (1 Peter 5:8), encouraged children to remain watchful, mindful of their choices, and grounded in their faith. Through prayer, Bible lessons, activities, and fellowship, the children were given opportunities to deepen their understanding of God's Word and strengthen their relationship with Christ.

Children and clergy.

Bringing our two church communities together was a tremendous blessing. The experience fostered fellowship, created new friendships, and reminded us of the beauty of growing together in our Orthodox Christian faith.

Faith in Action: Serving Others and Giving Back

An important part of our Sunday School vision is teaching our children that faith is not simply something we learn about; it is something we put into action. We believe that nurturing a relationship with Christ also means developing hearts that are compassionate, generous, and willing to serve others. Throughout the year, we have continued to emphasize the importance of mission work, outreach, and giving back to those in need.

Through our various outreach initiatives, we strive to help our students understand that even the smallest act of kindness can make a meaningful difference in someone's life.

Some of our mission-focused initiatives include:

• Thanksgiving Outreach: Sharing a Thanksgiving meal with a school in need, reminding our students of the importance of gratitude and ensuring that others feel cared for and remembered during the holiday season.

• Mission Work and School Outreach: Supporting a school in need through service initiatives that allow our students to recognize the importance of giving back and helping other children in our broader community.

Operation Christmas Child.

Operation Christmas Child: Participating in this wonderful initiative by filling shoeboxes with gifts and essential items for children in need. Each shoebox serves as a reminder that love, generosity, and the spirit of Christmas can reach children around the world.

• Food Drives: Encouraging students and families to come together to collect food for those experiencing hardship and food insecurity.

These opportunities help our children see that being a Christian means looking beyond ourselves and recognizing the needs of others. We want our students to grow into individuals who not only know the teachings of Christ but also live them through their actions.

As we often remind our students, we are called not only to receive God's love but to share that love with the world. Our hope is to cultivate a lifelong spirit of service, generosity, and compassion in every child we teach.

Looking Ahead: Same Faith, Brighter Hearts, Bigger Purpose

As we look toward the 2026–2027 Sunday School year, we are excited to embrace our new theme:

“Same Faith, Brighter Hearts, Bigger Purpose.”

This theme reflects our desire to remain firmly rooted in the unchanging truth of our Orthodox faith while nurturing

St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church 67 Golden Jubilee 1976 – 2026

Our Sunday School

hearts filled with Christ's love and inspiring our students to live with greater purpose. We hope to encourage our children to carry their faith beyond the classroom and into their homes, schools, friendships, and communities.

Our mission remains the same: to nurture a generation of children who know Christ, love Christ, and reflect Christ in all they do. Through the dedication of our teachers, the support of our families, and the grace of God, we look forward to another year of spiritual growth, meaningful fellowship, and service to others.

With Gratitude and Appreciation

As we reflect on this journey, we extend our heartfelt gratitude to Rev. Fr. Shibu Venad Mathai (Shibu Achen) for his unwavering love, dedication, and commitment to our children and the Sunday School ministry. His genuine love for our students, encouragement, and willingness to invest his time and heart in their spiritual growth have been a tremendous blessing to our community. His care for our children and passion for nurturing their faith have left a lasting impression on our Sunday School family. Shibu Achen, thank you for being such a special part of our children's spiritual journey. You will always hold a special place in our hearts.

We also extend a warm and heartfelt welcome to our new Achen, Rev. Fr. Eby Paulose. We look forward to working together as we continue to nurture the faith of our children and strengthen our Sunday School ministry. We pray that God will bless his ministry among us with wisdom, strength, and abundant grace.

To our dedicated teachers, students, parents, volunteers, and parish members, thank you for your countless contributions, encouragement, commitment and prayer. Your willingness to share your time, talents, and love makes this ministry possible.

Above all, we thank God for blessing our Sunday School with wonderful children, devoted families, and a community united in faith and purpose. Every lesson taught, every activity shared, and every act of service contributes to the spiritual foundation we are building in our children.

May we continue to grow in faith, abound in hope, and reflect the love of Christ in all that we do.

May God bless our Sunday School ministry today and in the years to come!

Through every season, one mission endures: helping our children know Christ, love Christ, and reflect Christ in all they do.

The Women Who Built Our Church: The Story of Morth Mariam Vanitha Samajam (MMVS)

The Women's Ministry of SGMOC

Long before it carried a name, the spirit of Morth Mariam Vanitha Samajam (MMVS) was already alive within St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church. From the very founding of the parish in 1976, the women of SGMOC gathered in one another's homes for worship and prayer, planting the seeds of a ministry that would grow alongside the church itself.

It was in 1982, when the North East American Diocese formally established MMVS at the diocesan level, that this quiet devotion found its official structure. The diocesan initiative gave rise to the MMVS wing within SGMOC, formalizing a ministry the women of the parish had already been living out for years.

The Initial Years

As a small women's ministry unit in its earliest days, MMVS was led by Very Rev. K. Mathai as President, supported by Rev. Fr. Paul Varki and Dn. Markose Mani, the late Mrs. Saramma Mathai, as its first Secretary, alongside Mrs. Aleyamma Mani, as its first Treasurer. When the official MMVS ministry was established at the NE American Diocese level in 1982, the SGMOC unit elected Mrs. Aleyamma Mani as Secretary and Mrs. Rachel Parel as Treasurer, marking the ministry's transition into its formal structure.

In its earliest years, MMVS took shape through simple, faithful routines that grounded the ministry in prayer and service. Monthly prayer meetings became a cornerstone of parish life, with members encouraged to share a message drawn from the Scripture portion they had read that morning — turning each gathering into a time of both personal reflection and communal prayer.

MMVS also took on the joyful responsibility of serving food after Holy Qurbana every Sunday. Nothing was ever ordered from outside; the food was cooked at home and brought to the church each Sunday morning, a personal offering of love and labor for the parish family.

During these formative years, MMVS members also attended an MMVS conference in New York, where their team won prizes in the quiz competition — a proud moment of fellowship alongside women from other parishes. Closer to home, MMVS helped decorate and arrange the dining room for weddings and baptisms, and some members gave their time to teaching Sunday school classes, nurturing the faith of the parish's youngest generation from the ministry's earliest days.

Faith at the Center of Everyday Life

The women of the parish were, in many cases, working multiple shifts to support their families — yet through it all, prayer, worship, and church remained at the very core of their lives. At home, they built consistent prayer routines and made it their mission to raise their children in the Orthodox faith, even while living far from their homeland. This quiet, steady discipline in the household became the foundation on which the next generation's faith was built.

Building a Lasting Structure

Over time, what began as informal gatherings of faith and service matured into a formally organized ministry. MMVS developed its own leadership structure, with a Secretary, Treasurer, and other committee members guiding its work. This newly formed committee went on to establish an annual calendar of events for the ministry, including biweekly prayer meetings held at the church and monthly prayer meetings hosted in the homes of members — carrying forward the very tradition of home-based worship and fellowship on which MMVS was first built.

St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church 70 Golden Jubilee 1976 – 2026

Marth Mariam Vanitha Samajam

Sacrifice and Support for a Growing Church

As a small parish working to establish itself, SGMOC relied heavily on the generosity of its members — and the women of MMVS were at the forefront of that effort. The women contributed to the parish building fund in multiple ways over the years. Through a one-day salary donation drive, the stained glass windows for the church were purchased in full. They traveled to various cities and churches to help raise funds toward establishing a new church home in Bensalem, PA. Through MMVS subscriptions and other fundraising efforts, the ministry also funded a variety of other items for the new building including the kitchen and the most recent contribution being the altar candlesticks. Their willingness to give both their time and resources reflected a deep investment in the parish's future.

Their service was not limited to their own community. The Ministry continues to support the education of two girls in India. Various other charity and mission projects provide support to many families in need both in India and in the United States— a reflection of the Orthodox call to serve beyond the walls of the church.

MMVS 40th Year Celebration – 2022

In 2022, the Northeast American Diocese MMVS celebrated its 40th anniversary, marking the milestone with several diocesan events. As part of this observance, founding MMVS members from each parish — those serving since 1982 — were formally honored.

At our parish, a special recognition ceremony was held on Sunday, August 28, 2022, honoring 19 long-standing MMVS members. Sunday school children escorted each honoree with a rose as a gesture of love and respect, and the vicar presented a shawl to acknowledge their decades of dedicated service to MMVS.

These members were also recognized at the Diocesan Celebration on October 1, 2022, held at St. Thomas Indian Orthodox Church, Unruh, where they received a custom plaque and shawl.

For the Diocese's 40th-year charity initiative, our parish raised $3,160 through raffle sales. In addition, one MMVS member personally contributed $1,500 to sponsor a student, offered as an individual anonymous donation.

Long-serving MMVS members honored at our parish, August 28, 2022.

MMVS in Its Current Form

Since 2011, under the guidance of Rev. Fr. Shibu Mathai, who serves as President, MMVS has continued to grow in faith and purpose. At its heart, MMVS remains a ministry centered on prayer and worship. This continues to be the main focus of the group, just as it was in its earliest days — grounding every act of service in a life of faith. Members also lend their voices to the church choir, adding to the worship life of the parish.

Today, MMVS remains united in service to the church, ready to step in wherever the need arises. The ministry continues to support all major parish activities, including Great Lent and Holy Week observances, Parish Day, the church picnic, Harvest Festival, Heritage Day, the Perunal Celebration, and Christmas festivities.

Beyond the parish, MMVS members actively participate in ecumenical programs such as the World Day of Prayer, Choir Fest, and Christmas Fest, building fellowship and connection with the broader Christian community. Our MMVS members also take part in the annual Diocese Bible Quiz, winning prizes on many occasions, as well as the Diocese Annual Conference and Talent Show, and the Diocese Retreat at HTRC. The 2026 Golden Jubilee year was especially memorable, as our Bible Quiz team brought great pride to SGMOC by winning 1st prize among 29 teams from across the Diocese.

St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church 71 Golden Jubilee 1976 – 2026

Marth Mariam Vanitha Samajam

Women in Church and Lay Leadership Roles

As opportunities opened for women to take on greater roles in parish governance, the women of SGMOC were quick to step forward. When women were given a seat in the General Body meetings and allowed to be part of the Church Committee, our women immediately took on multiple leadership roles within the core team, the Board, and various committees.

MMVS members also play pivotal roles at the Philadelphia Area and Northeast American Diocese levels. Women from our parish have served as Area Coordinator and Area Representative. At the Diocese level, our women have held key leadership positions, including Joint Secretary and Divyabodhanam Coordinator, among other roles — a testament to the strength and depth of leadership this ministry has cultivated over the decades.

Our women have also held numerous leadership positions across various ministries of the NE American Diocese, including Diocese Sunday School, GROW, MGOCSM, and other ministries — carrying the spirit of MMVS's service and leadership into every corner of the wider church community.

This leadership has not come at the expense of balance, but through it. The women of our parish carry their faith into every part of life. They manage demanding responsibilities outside the home, yet remain steady pillars at church — present in prayer, generous with their time, and faithful in service. Many have skillfully balanced busy careers with active roles at church, prayerfully bringing sound work ethics into their ministry, while carrying the lessons of their faith back into their daily lives.

A Legacy That Continues

Over the last 50 years, the women of SGMOC have been a constant, steady presence in the life of the parish — carrying it forward in prayer, service, sacrifice, and leadership. What began in 1976 as informal home prayer gatherings grew into a formally established ministry, built on faithful prayer routines, quiet service, selfless charity and mission activities and generous sacrifice for the church's growth, even as many balance demanding careers and home. Today, the ministry remains centered on prayer and worship, supporting every major parish and community event, and continues to be recognized as a model unit within the Diocese — a legacy carried forward with each new generation.

Good Samaritan Mission

ദൈവ നാമത്തിനു മഹത്വം

കഴിഞ്ഞ പത്തു വർഷമായി നമ്മുടെ ഇടവകയിൽ പ്രവർത്തിച്ചു വരുന്ന ഒരു ആത്മീക പ്രസ്ഥാനം ആണ് Good Samaritan Mission. എല്ലാ വ്യാഴാഴ്ചകളിലും രാവിലെ പത്തു മണിമുതൽ ഞങ്ങൾ പ്രാർത്ഥനകൂട്ടമായി കൂടിവരുന്നു. ചില പ്രത്യേക സാഹചര്യങ്ങളിൽ മാത്രമേ ഈ കൂട്ടായ്മക്ക് മുടക്കം ഉണ്ടായിട്ടുള്ളൂ. ഈ കൂട്ടയ്മയിൽ വേദ പുസ്തകത്തിൽ നിന്നും പുതിയ നിയമവും പഴയ നിയമവും എല്ലാവരും വായിക്കുകയും, വചനം പഠിക്കുകയും ചെയ്യും. ഞങ്ങൾ വേദപുസ്തകം മുഴുവനും ഒരു പ്രാവശ്യം വായിച്ചു കഴിഞ്ഞു. ഇനിയും തുടർന്നു കൊണ്ടിരിക്കുന്നു. സാഹചര്യം അനുസരിച്ചുള്ള വിവരണങ്ങളും പൊരുളുകളും ഷിബു അച്ചനും സീനാ മാത്യു വും വിസിറ്റ് ചെയ്യുന്ന തിരുമേനിമാരും അച്ചന്മാരും വിശദീകരിച്ചു തരും.

നമ്മുടെ അറിവിലും അല്ലാതെയുമുള്ള അനേകരുടെ വിവിധങ്ങളായ ആവശ്യങ്ങൾക്കുവേണ്ടി പ്രാർത്ഥിക്കുന്നത് വളരെ അനുഗ്രഹമാണ്.

ഈ കൂട്ടായ്മയിൽ കൂടി പല വിധത്തിലുള്ള സഹായങ്ങൾ പലർക്കും നാട്ടിൽ ചെയ്യുവാൻ ദൈവം സഹായിച്ചു. ഈ സഹായങ്ങൾ തുടർന്നു കൊണ്ടു പോകുവാൻ ദൈവം അനുവദിക്കട്ടെ എന്ന് പ്രാർത്ഥിക്കുന്നു.

ഷിബു അച്ചൻ്റെ അനുവാദത്തോടുകൂടി ഞങ്ങൾ പലപ്പോഴും ഞങ്ങളുടെ അനുഭവ സാക്ഷ്യങ്ങൾ പങ്കുവെച്ചിട്ടുണ്ട്. "ജീവിതം നമ്മളെ എന്തൊക്കെ പഠിപ്പിച്ചു; നമ്മൾ എന്തെല്ലാം പഠിച്ചു"എന്നുള്ള ഒരു വിഷയം അച്ചൻ ഞങ്ങൾക്ക് തന്നു. എല്ലാവർക്കും ഓരോ ആഴ്ച്ച ഇതിനെക്കുറിച്ചു അവതരിപ്പിക്കാൻ അവസരം അനുവദിച്ചു. പലരും ഈ വിഷയം അവതരിപ്പിച്ചപ്പോൾ പുതിയ അറിവുകളും അനുഭവങ്ങളും വളരെ ലഭിക്കുവാൻ സാധിച്ചു.

ഒരു സാധാരണ കർഷക കുടുംബത്തിൽ അഞ്ചു മക്കളിൽ രണ്ടാമനായ എനിക്കുണ്ടായ അനുഭവങ്ങൾ പറയുവാൻ സാധിച്ചു. രാവിലെ അഞ്ചു മണിക്ക് പ്രാർത്ഥിക്കാൻ താമസിച്ചു പോയാൽ തണുത്ത വെള്ളം തലയിൽ ഒഴിക്കുക എന്ന ശിക്ഷ ലഭിച്ചിട്ടുണ്ട്. അന്ന് പിതാവിനോട് ദേഷ്യം മനസ്സിൽ തോന്നിയത് വളരെ തെറ്റാണെന്നു ഇപ്പോൾ തോന്നുന്നു.

പ്രാർത്ഥന: എപ്പോഴും പ്രാര്ഥനയോടു കൂടി തുടക്കം കുറിക്കണം എന്നുള്ള ഉപദേശം പിതാവിൽ നിന്നും പഠിച്ചു.

അച്ചടക്കം: ഞാൻ പഠിച്ച സ്കൂളിൽ അര മണിക്കൂർ വേദ പഠനം ക്രിസ്ത്യൻ കുട്ടികൾക്ക് നിർബന്ധമായിരുന്നു. അഞ്ചു മിനിറ്റ് എല്ലാ കുട്ടികളും പിൻ-ഡ്രോപ്പ് സൈലെൻസിൽ ആയിരിക്കണം എന്നുള്ളത് തെറ്റിയാൽ ശിക്ഷ വളരെ കഠിനമായിരുന്നു.

അനുസരണം: സ്കൂൾ പ്രധാന റോഡിൽ നിന്നും വളരെ ഉയരത്തിൽ ആയിരുന്നു, പരുപരുത്ത കാട്ടു കല്ലു കൊണ്ട് നിർമ്മിച്ച വഴിയിൽകൂടി ഓടി ഇറങ്ങരുത് എന്നുള്ള പിതാവിൻ്റെ കർശന ഉപദേശത്തെ അനുസരിക്കാതെ എപ്പോഴും ഓടി ഇറങ്ങുമായിരുന്നു. കാൽ തെറ്റി ഒരു പ്രാവശ്യം മുകളിൽ നിന്നും ശയന പ്രദക്ഷിണം നടത്തി പ്രധാന റോഡിൽ വന്നു വീണപ്പോൾ ശരീരത്തിൻ്റെ പല ഭാഗത്തും തൊലി നഷ്ടപെട്ടിരുന്നു. രണ്ടു കൂട്ടുകാർ താങ്ങി എടുത്തു കൊണ്ട് ഭവനത്തിൽ വന്നപ്പോൾ പിതാവിൻ്റെ ശിക്ഷ അതിലും വേദനാത്മകമായിരുന്നു. തെറ്റു കണ്ടാൽ ശിക്ഷിക്കാനും തിരുത്താനും അയൽക്കാരും പരിചയക്കാരും ഉണ്ടായിരുന്നതു കാരണം പല തെറ്റുകളിൽ നിന്നും ഒഴിഞ്ഞിരിക്കാൻ സാധിച്ചു.

പുതിയ നിയമത്തിൽ ന്യായശാസ്ത്രിയും കർത്താവും തമ്മിലുള്ള സംഭാഷണത്തിൻ്റെ ഒടുവിൽ കർത്താവു അവനോടു പറയുന്നു "നീ ദൈവരാജ്യത്തിൽ നിന്നും അകന്നവനല്ല."ദൈവരാജ്യത്തിൽ പ്രവേശിക്കണമെങ്കിൽ പ്രാര്ഥനയെന്ന താക്കോൽ ആവശ്യമാണ്. നമ്മുടെ എല്ലാവരുടേയും കൈവശമുള്ള ഈ താക്കോൽ വേണ്ട സമയത്തു ഉപയോഗിച്ചില്ലാ എങ്കിൽ അകത്തു പ്രവേശിക്കാൻ കഴിയാത്ത കന്യകമാരെ പോലെ ആയിത്തീരും.

നമ്മുടെ കർത്താവു കുരിശിൽ മരിച്ചു ഉയർത്തെഴുന്നേറ്റു നമുക്ക് ഭവനം ഒരുക്കുവാൻ സ്വർഗ്ഗത്തിലേക്ക് പോയിരിക്കുകയാണ്. നമ്മളെ ചേർക്കുവാൻ വേഗം വരുന്നു. അതിൻ്റെ എല്ലാ ലക്ഷണങ്ങളും കണ്ടു കഴിഞ്ഞു. സമയം ഇനിയും അധികമില്ല. മനസാന്തരപ്പെടുവിൻ. നമ്മുടെ തെറ്റുകൾ ദൈവസന്നിധിൽ ഏറ്റു പറഞ്ഞു പാപ ക്ഷമ പ്രാപിച്ചു ദൈവത്തോടു നിരന്നു കൊൾവീൻ.

നമ്മുടെ ഇടവകയുടെ അൻപതാം വാർഷീകം ആഘോഷിക്കുന്ന ഈ സമയത്തു GSM ൻ്റെ എല്ലാവിധ ആശംസകളും പ്രാർത്ഥനയും അർപ്പിക്കുന്നു.

പ്രാർത്ഥനയോടുകൂടി

Logos Ministry

Living, Guarding, and Proclaiming the Word of God

“The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son, who came from the Father, full of grace and truth.” — John 1:14

The LOGOS Ministry is a dedicated community of young adult Orthodox believers (ages 18+) at St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church devoted to growing together in fellowship, love, and obedience to Jesus Christ. Taking its name from the Greek word for "Word," LOGOS centers its mission on Christ, the incarnate Word of God. As young adults navigating the challenges of a modern world, our desire is to fulfill our calling as an edifying force for both our parish community and the broader society.

Our ministry is anchored in five foundational pillars reflected in our name: Loving each other and our surrounding community, Offering service and digital outreach, Guarding and defending our Orthodox faith, Obeying Christ's commandments in daily life, and Sanctifying our lives through spiritual disciplines to draw closer to God. We put these principles into action through bi-weekly Bible studies and small-group discussions rooted in Holy Scripture and Church Fathers. Additionally, through our social media presence, we extend Orthodox teaching beyond the church walls, offering clear and practical reflections for daily life.

Beyond our internal fellowship, LOGOS is deeply committed to mentoring the next generation. We have a vision to create a structured mentorship program organized in conjunction with the Sunday School ministry in the near future. LOGOS members would pair with high school students to provide spiritual guidance, Christian discipleship, and a safe space for honest conversation during pivotal life transitions.

We invite all young adults to join us as we encourage one another to live as faithful doers of the Word.

GROW

God Renewing Orthodox Women

G.R.O.W. Ministry Celebrates 15 Years: DKNE Camp 2026

In celebration of its 15th anniversary, G.R.O.W. Ministry hosted the Daughters of the King of the Northeast (DKNE) three-day camp at the Holy Transfiguration Retreat Center. Centered on the theme “Vessels of Purpose” from 2 Corinthians 4:7, the camp was a time of faith, sisterhood, fellowship, and spiritual renewal.

The main speaker for the DKNE Camp was Dr. Eugenia Constantinou. Dr. Constantinou delivered an engaging session, teaching the women about the powerful significance of the theme and importance of Christ’s calling of women apostles and disciples. She taught that purpose is ultimately found in our identity rooted in Christ and not in what the world believes we are. Through engaging teachings, interactive discussions, games, and hands-on clay activities, the women were encouraged to reflect on their God-given purpose, share their experiences, and grow deeper in their faith.

This year, we were especially blessed to have 15 women from SGMOC participate in the camp. The experience provided our sisters with a wonderful opportunity to reconnect, strengthen friendships, and experience spiritual renewal. The meaningful conversations and shared reflections offered encouragement and a deeper understanding of what it means to live as vessels of God’s purpose. In addition to the speaker sessions and discussions, G.R.O.W. Ministry hosted a beautiful Gala Dinner celebrating 15 years of God’s faithfulness. It was a special opportunity to honor the past, present, and future as well as inspire new generations to come forward and serve.

The retreat culminated with Holy Qurbana on Sunday with His Grace Zachariah Mar Nicholovos, reminding everyone that Christ remains at the center of their journey. As each participant returned home, they carried cherished memories, strengthened friendships, renewed faith, and a deeper commitment to serve as a Daughter of the King, shining God’s light wherever He leads. We pray that younger generations will continue to embrace this ministry, build upon the strong foundation laid by those before them, and carry forward its mission of nurturing faith, sisterhood, and spiritual growth for years to come.

St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church 78 Golden Jubilee 1976 – 2026

GROW Sprouts

God Renewing Orthodox Women

G.R.O.W. Sprouts is a focused ministry for girls ages 6–12, bringing together families from Orthodox churches across the Philadelphia area. Connected with GROW and Sunday School, the ministry provides a welcoming community where girls can grow in faith, fellowship, friendship, charity, and service, while strengthening their relationship with Christ and the Orthodox Church.

Our Spiritual Mentors include Rev. Fr. Vijay Thomas, Rev. Fr. Timothy (Tenny) Thomas, and Very Rev. Geevarghese Ramban (Rev. Fr. Shibu V. Mathai), and our Co-Leads are Dr. Silvi Chacko and Princy Mathai.

Throughout the last couple of years, activities included daily Lenten devotionals, Mom & GROW Sprouts fellowships, a visit to Holy Protection Orthodox Monastery, charity food-packing (for Caring for Friends), the Feast Day celebration of St. Sophia, painting an icon, participation in the Diocesan Sunday School Talent Show, and a year-end Friendsgiving celebration.

Together, these activities help GROW Sprouts create a community of faith, giving young girls opportunities to deepen their relationship with Christ, build lasting friendships, learn the importance of charity and volunteer service, and grow within the Orthodox faith.

Choir

Serving God through music and worship

“Sing to the Lord a new song; sing to the Lord, all the earth.”

— Psalm 96:1

The Church Choir Ministry is a dedicated group of Orthodox believers who use their God-given musical talents to glorify God, lead the congregation, and enhance the worship experience. As an essential part of our Orthodox tradition, the choir helps create an atmosphere that draws the congregation closer to God’s presence during the Divine Liturgy.

Orthodox tones and musical settings are among the most beautiful in the world. As choir members, we honor God with humility and dedication, creating an uplifting atmosphere through well-sung hymns during Holy Qurbana that encourages worshippers to deeply immerse themselves in the liturgy.

Our mission is to glorify God with our voices. Beyond the beauty of the music, we aim to convey the deeper meaning of what is sung to lead the congregation in meaningful worship. We invite everyone to join us in enriching the spiritual life of our SGMOC community.

SGMOC Chenda Family

Preserving a Rich Cultural Heritage

Chenda and Kerala Culture

The chenda, a cylindrical percussion instrument from Kerala, is one of the most celebrated symbols of Kerala’s cultural heritage, long associated with festivals, ceremonial processions and classical arts such as Kathakali. Among the Malayali diaspora it remains a powerful connection to home, and the synchronized rhythms of the chenda melam symbolize unity, discipline and shared participation.

Chenda Comes to SGMOC

Chenda performances have long been part of parish celebrations at SGMOC. The SGMOC Chenda Team was formally established in 2015 with the support of Rev. Fr. Shibu Venad Mathai, led by Thomas O. Abraham, Biju Mani and Biju Chacko. Training began under Gopi Ashan of Delaware and, after his passing, continued under Akash Ashan of Philadelphia. About twenty-five chendas were brought from Thrissur, Kerala, giving the parish a full ensemble. In loving remembrance, our Chenda team pays tribute to our dear former Chenda family member, Manoj Ninan.

Growing Over the Years

The team soon became an integral part of the Parish Day festivities in May and the Perunnal in November. Usha Philipose’s leadership and encouragement strengthened participation, and in recent years Daya Kappil and John Kappil, who study chenda at a professional training center, have continued the training. Today the ensemble welcomes men, women, youth and children, keeping a treasured tradition alive and connecting generations, in Kerala and around the world. Special thanks and congratulations to our Metropolitan-designate, Very Rev. Geevarghese Ramban; may God bless his new journey. Under the new church leadership of Rev. Fr. Eby Paulose, we look forward to many exciting years ahead.

St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church 83 Golden Jubilee 1976 – 2026

Acolytes

Faithfully Serving at the Holy Altar

The Acolyte Ministry of SGMOC Bensalem

The Acolyte Ministry of St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church (SGMOC), Bensalem, stands as a testament to faith, devotion, and the enduring legacy of service to the Holy Church. Founded by Very Rev. K. Mathai Cor Episcopos, this ministry was established with a vision to nurture young men in the sacred traditions of the Malankara Orthodox Church and instill in them a deep reverence for the Holy Altar. Through the years, generations of acolytes have faithfully served in the divine liturgy, carrying forward a tradition rooted in prayer, discipline, humility, and unwavering devotion to Christ and His Church.

This legacy has been strengthened and enriched through the dedicated leadership of Rev. Fr. Shibu Mathai, under whose guidance the ministry continued to grow and flourish. We lovingly remember Rev. Fr. Paul Varki and Rev. Dn. Markose Mani, of blessed memory, whose lives, service, and spiritual contributions remain an enduring part of our parish’s history. Their faithful witness and dedication helped shape the spiritual foundation upon which future generations continue to build. As we celebrate the Golden Jubilee of SGMOC, we honor these servants of God and all those who have devoted their time, talents, and hearts to the sacred calling of serving at the Holy Altar.

Today, under the leadership and spiritual guidance of Rev. Fr. Eby Paulose, the Acolyte Ministry looks toward a future filled with renewed purpose, deeper faith, and greater commitment. With Achen’s guidance, encouragement, and vision, we pray that this ministry will flourish even more powerfully, raising generations of faithful servants who will uphold the sacred traditions of our Church and boldly carry its spiritual legacy into the future. As we honor fifty years of God’s faithfulness, may the acolytes of SGMOC continue to stand as a living testimony to the power of faith, the beauty of service, and the enduring strength of a Church rooted in Christ. May God bless this ministry abundantly and guide it from strength to strength for generations to come.

SGMOC Mission Board

Our Mission Journey, 2018 to 2026

Highlights from the Sunday School Mission Team and the SGMOC Mission Board

“…proclaim liberty throughout all the land unto all the inhabitants thereof: it shall be a jubilee unto you.” — Leviticus 25:10

A Jubilee Welcome

In Scripture, a jubilee is a season of rejoicing and restoration. It is a time when God’s people remember that everything they hold is a gift, open their hands, and share with their neighbors (Leviticus 25). As we celebrate this Jubilee, we look back on nine years of mission work at St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church (SGMOC) in Bensalem, and we see that same spirit at work.

It shows in backpacks packed for children in Pennsylvania and sent to Kerala during floods, in blankets crafted at fellowship hall tables, in shoeboxes carried to the church by small hands, supporting the back to school projects, in a Thanksgiving table set for the whole community and appreciating our local EMT and Police department and mega mission projects such as supporting Rise against Hunger. What began as a handful of Sunday School service days has grown into a parish-wide ministry of mercy which is the Mission Board.

Our Mission Board: Purpose and Model

The work began with the Sunday School Mission Team and grew into a parish-wide Mission Team in 2023. The idea for a Mission Board took shape in 2024 as the parish looked for a way to coordinate charitable work across its ministries. In 2025, the SGMOC Mission Board was officially formed, bringing together representatives from across the parish.

The Board is a group of parish volunteers who coordinate the mission activities of our church. Its purpose is simple: to bring the charitable work of our ministries together in one prayerful effort so that our gifts reach people in need. Through this collaboration, the parish supports medical missions and other works of charity.

Under the spiritual guidance of our clergy, Rev. Fr. Shibu Venad Mathai and our current Vicar, Rev. Fr. Eby Paulose, ministry representatives plan, coordinate and lead mission activities. Each project has its own lead and team. The Managing Committee and the Board review and approve charity applications, and every member of the parish is invited to serve as a volunteer.

A Reflection

“And do not forget to do good and to share with others, for with such sacrifices God is pleased.”

— Hebrews 13:16

Year by Year: 2018 to 2026

2018 — Planting the Seeds

The story begins with the Sunday School Mission Team and a simple conviction: that children learn faith best by serving. In March, our Sunday School held a Day of Service, preparing and serving food at a Philadelphia homeless shelter run by

St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church 85 Golden Jubilee 1976 – 2026

SGMOC Mission Board

Project Home. That same month, children and parents wrote cards of encouragement and prayer for the students, staff and families of Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Florida, and sent them in a Box of Hope and Support.

In September we launched the Backpack Project for deserving children in Kerala who were affected by the floods and they were blessed by H.H. BASELIOS MAR THOMA PAULOSE II (BAVA THIRUMENI). In November we prepared and served a Thanksgiving meal to students and parents at Snyder-Girotti Elementary School. By December, 288 backpacks had been distributed in the USA and Kerala, reaching Snyder-Girotti Elementary, the ARDRA Foundation in Kerala and schools in Wayanad. A winter jacket drive supported AHTN, Bucks County and Snyder-Girotti Elementary, with thermals going to AHTN, and the season closed with Christmas caroling and craft-making with the residents of Woodbourne senior home.

“Let us not love with words or speech but with actions and in truth.”

— 1 John 3:18

2019 — A Mission Takes Shape

On September 29, 2019, the Sunday School Mission Team gathered at the SGMOC Harvest Festival and shared a bold plan: six themed ministries offering “opportunities for children of all ages to volunteer time and talents for the Kingdom of God.” The team was led by Rev. Shibu V. Mathai, with Sunday School Principal Reny Biju and Mission Coordinator Dr. Silvi Chacko, together with Caroline Varughese, Neethu Varghese, Jessy Mathai, Shainey Jacob, Shyno Thomas, Sunitha Zachariah, Siji John, Sherin Kurian and Mable Philip.

Our Sunday School children prepared 150 care packages every quarter for children served by the Bucks County Intermediate Unit, and invited volunteers to MANNA on Main Street in Lansdale. Youth ages 12 and older helped prepare and serve meals at St. Francis Inn Ministries in Philadelphia. In November the team organized a Rise Against Hunger meal packing at SGMOC, described in our feature below.

Hope & Love made 26 blankets for Project Linus and thanked the Bensalem Police Department with a card, treats, snacks and a tour of the station. Helping Hands cleaned the Mission Center and church kitchen. Gifts of Love set a goal of at least 100 Operation Christmas Child shoeboxes, teaching our children to love “not in word or tongue” but in “deed and truth,” and our Back to School drive supplied Loesche Elementary School with uniforms for 20 children and stationery for 50, and gave folders for 128 students plus nurse’s office supplies to the Philadelphia girls’ high school.

“I tell you the truth, anyone who gives you a cup of water in my name because you belong to Christ will certainly not lose his reward.”

— Mark 9:41

2020 — Serving Through the Pandemic

When the world closed its doors, our mission did not. The Sunday School Mission Team moved its work onto Zoom calls, phone calls and front porches, and found new ways to serve while keeping one another safe.

Early in the year, we distributed warmers through AHTN and returned in the fall with more body warmers. From July through December, we provided pizza every month for Bensalem’s first responders. We also supported 15 Bensalem families with monthly meals through the Ivins Outreach Center, an effort that continued into the fall.

From July 5 to August 28, our eight-week Malayalam Vidhyalam brought 45 students and 15 teachers together to learn spoken Malayalam, prayers, songs and family relationships, and to follow recipes through cooking videos. Through the CARES points program, children earned points for acts of kindness, from sending get-well cards and helping neighbors with yard work to playing piano over Zoom or chalking an encouraging note on a driveway.

St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church 87 Golden Jubilee 1976 – 2026

In the fall, we collected Operation Christmas Child shoeboxes, made 30 blankets for Project Linus and held sock and winter coat drives. Children exchanged letters and cards with Woodbourne Nursing Home residents and sang Christmas carols for them virtually. We also continued sponsoring a child in India.

During that same period, the team collected and delivered new and gently used clothing for Afghan refugee families in collaboration with The Wardrobe, Cradles and Crayons, and Replay.

“In a world where you can be anything, be kind.”

— Mother Teresa, quoted in our CARES points program

Distance changed how we served, never why we served. In the hardest season many of us have known, our children discovered that kindness needs no building, only a willing heart.

Our students exchanged letters with seniors at Woodbourne Nursing Home from January through December. In February, they tucked snacks and handwritten notes into bags of socks for the Bucks County Homeless Shelter as part of the winter coat and sock drive. In April, they collected children’s and adult diapers and wipes in partnership with the Philadelphia Diaper Bank. That spring, students also collected personal hygiene items and raised funds through a mug-painting fundraiser to purchase medical supplies, baby essentials and mobility aids for people affected by the war in Ukraine, including refugees.

In July and August, optional contributions from the summer Malayalam School helped send clothing and school supplies to children in tribal communities in India, with our Vicar, Rev. Fr. Shibu Venad Mathai, leading the project. In September, the Sunday School donated school supplies to four Philadelphia-area schools. We also continued providing monthly pizza lunches for Bensalem Police and emergency personnel.

In November, our children, parents and teachers returned in person to serve a Thanksgiving meal to families in need. In December, students and families donated 100 Operation Christmas Child shoeboxes, and our students shared songs and skits with Woodbourne residents in a virtual Christmas celebration.

“Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.”

— Matthew 25:40

A handwritten letter may seem small. To a senior who had gone months without a visitor, it was a visit.

Feature: Rise Against Hunger

Rise Against Hunger is an international hunger relief organization that coordinates the packaging and distribution of food and other life-changing aid to people in developing nations. Our parish has joined its mission twice in this record, and each time with the same invitation printed on our flyer: #ItStartsWithAMeal, and it starts with you.

November 16, 2019: Pack 10,152 Meals

The Fish & Loaves team, led by Neethu Varghese, hosted a meal-packing event at SGMOC from 8 AM to 12:30 PM, calling for 100 volunteers and setting a goal of packing 10,152 meals to “make a difference in a family’s life.”

St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church 93 Golden Jubilee 1976 – 2026

September 2023: Sponsor, Paint, Pack

In 2023, the parish once again partnered with Rise Against Hunger, bringing the community together through fundraising, creative activities, donations and hands-on service to support the goal of providing 20,000 meals. Families participated in a special painting event featuring mugs and bowls, raising $1,075 for the meal-packing initiative. The effort culminated on September 30, when volunteers packed 20,088 meals, exceeding the 20,000-meal goal and demonstrating the parish’s continued commitment to fighting hunger through generosity, fellowship and community service.

Parish volunteers packing meals at the Rise Against Hunger event, September 2023.

The icon of the feeding of the multitude that graces our Mission Board reports reminds us that Christ takes what we offer, however small, and multiplies it. A 39-cent meal is a small offering. Ten thousand of them are a feast.

A Jubilee Reflection

A jubilee asks us to pause, give thanks and look at what God has done through ordinary people with open hands. As we look back on nine years of mission, we give thanks to those whose faithfulness has carried this work.

To our clergy, especially our Vicar, Rev. Fr. Eby Paulose, Very Rev. Geevarghese Ramban (Rev. Fr. Shibu Venad Mathai), whose spiritual guidance and leadership have rooted every project in prayer, and to our Associate Minister, Mrs. Ceena Mathew, we offer our gratitude and our love.

To our ministry leaders, the Mission Board’s Ministry Representatives and the many project leads and teams who planned, phoned, packed and drove: Joe John, Mathew M. Kurian, Dr. Jesty Moses, Alex Thankachan and Thomas Joseph who serve as Managing Committee and Board representatives and authored the annual reports with Vincy Wilson;

St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church 100 Golden Jubilee 1976 – 2026

SGMOC Mission Board

the leaders of the Sunday School Mission Team since 2018, including Dr. Silvi Chacko, Reny Biju, Vincy Wilson and Caroline Varughese; and the leads of MMVS, GSM, the Men’s Forum, G.R.O.W, S.T.G., Youth League and the Acolytes. Thank you for turning good intentions into good works.

Through the Mission Board, the generosity of our ministries became a shared effort of service. In 2024, the Managing Committee and Board approved 16 charity applications totaling $12,000 in donations, while MMVS, GSM, Sunday School and Youth League held 17 charity drives and events totaling approximately $15,000. In 2025, the parish contributed approximately $25,000 toward charitable efforts.

Behind these figures are blankets made for children, meals shared with hungry neighbors, school supplies packed with care, diapers provided to families, and visits that brought joy to seniors. From Project Linus and Mother of Mercy House to our Back-to-School, Thanksgiving and Christmas outreach, each project reflects the compassion of our parish and the faithful work of those who served.

These accomplishments stand as a testament to the parish’s deep-rooted commitment to living out the call to charity and compassion. The generosity of our members, both in financial contributions and active participation, has made a lasting impact on countless lives.

To our children, who have packed shoeboxes since 2013, assembled care packages, sung carols, served Thanksgiving meals and made blankets. You remind us that even small hands can make a lasting impact.

St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church 101 Golden Jubilee 1976 – 2026

SGMOC Mission Board

To our families, who gave generously, brought their children to serve, and delivered supplies to schools. The heart of this mission is the family.

And to our volunteers, all members of SGMOC, whose time, effort and faithful stewardship have been the driving force behind the Mission Board: thank you. Your work has touched hundreds of lives locally and around the world, and thousands through our partners.

A Closing Prayer

Lord Jesus Christ, You multiplied the loaves and fed the multitude. Receive the small gifts we have offered in Your name, bless the hands that gave them, and keep us ever faithful to proclaim, by our deeds, a Jubilee of mercy for all. Amen.

St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church 106 Golden Jubilee 1976 – 2026

A Tribute to Rev. Fr. Dr. Paul Varki

Proof copy

Rev. Fr. Dr. Paul Varki (formerly Dn. Paul Varki) faithfully served the Malankara Orthodox Church throughout his life. As we celebrate our Golden Jubilee, we lovingly remember a man whose devotion, humility, and steadfast service shaped the earliest foundations of our community.

Ordained as a deacon at age 18 by His Holiness Baselios Geevarghese II, he came to the United States in 1957 for higher studies. He pursued advanced academic work—including studies at Princeton University—and later earned a doctorate in Psychology. While serving as a Board-certified Psychologist for the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, he quietly nurtured the spiritual life of Malayalee Orthodox Christians in the region.

In 1965, he helped organize monthly worship at Asbury Church, hosting clergy from multiple denominations. This ecumenical fellowship became a spiritual home for Orthodox, Marthoma, Catholic, CSI, and other Kerala Christians for eleven years.

A turning point came in 1976, when he invited Rev. Fr. K. Mathai to lead Holy Week services. The overwhelming response led to the formation of the first Orthodox parish in Philadelphia. He later wrote to the Catholicos requesting authorization for a parish—resulting in the establishment of St. Thomas Orthodox Church of India (STOCI) on October 10, 1976.

The parish grew steadily, acquiring its first church building in Torresdale in 1984 and later building a new church in Bensalem, consecrated in 2009. As the new church neared completion, Paul Varki Achen reflected on the community’s journey with a joyful Malayalam poem:

അറുപത്തിനാലിൽ വിശ്വാസികൾ നട്ട മുന്തിരി വെസ്റ്റ് ഫിലിയിൽ
സെൻറ്‌ തോമസ് ആയി വന്നെല്ലോ
അതിനെ നനച്ചു വളർത്തി നാം സെൻറ്‌ ഗ്രീഗോറിയോസ് ആയി
ടോറസ്ഡെയിലിൽ ശോഭിച്ചു
[വീണ്ടും] ചേരുക നീ എൻ മാനസമേ
ബെൻസലേമിലെ നിലയത്തിൽ
പരുമല മരുവും തിരുമേനി വന്നു വസിക്കുന്നീ നാളിൽ
ഇന്നീ ജനന പെരുന്നാളിൽ
നാഥാ കരുണാ സാഗരമേ ഓർക്കണമേ നിൻ ജനതതിയെ

Rev. Fr. Dr. Paul Varki’s legacy is one of faithfulness, perseverance, and love. He helped build a community before there was a parish, welcomed clergy before there was a resident priest, and fostered unity long before there were church buildings. His memory remains a blessing to every Orthodox family in Greater Philadelphia.

— Mariamma Varki

A Journey of Faith,
Love, and Gratitude

Over the years, SGMOC has played a crucial role in our lives, nurturing our faith and guiding us along our spiritual journey. We have celebrated many joyful milestones together and have also faced our share of challenges along the way. Throughout these years, we have grown to cherish the blessing of having a loving and supportive church family, whose presence has been especially meaningful during challenging times.

We are deeply thankful for all the love, prayers, guidance, and support we have received from clergy, especially Mathai Achen, Shibu Achen, and the entire SGMOC family. Their care and spiritual guidance, together with the friendship and fellowship of our parish community, have been a source of strength and encouragement to our family.

As we happily celebrate SGMOC’s Golden Jubilee, we give thanks to God for the many blessings, treasured memories, and lasting friendships that have been such a meaningful part of our lives. May God continue to shower His blessings upon our parish, guide us in our journey, strengthen the bonds of faith and fellowship among us, and unite us as one community for generations to come.

The Sign of the Cross:
A Prayer in Every Moment

By Jonathan Chacko

Have you ever wondered why we make the Sign of the Cross before meals, when setting out on a journey, or before going to bed? The Sign of the Cross is one of the shortest and most meaningful prayers which symbolizes the Crucifixion and Resurrection of Jesus Christ. It reminds us of God’s constant presence, love, and protection in our lives.

We should make it a habit to make the Sign of the Cross not only before important events, but every significant moment in our daily lives. It serves as a reminder to place our trust in God and seek His guidance and protection as we face life’s challenges. It also reminds us of His promise to remain with us and guide us away from evil.

Whenever we make the Sign of the Cross, we should also remember those who are less fortunate, offer prayers for them, and give thanks to God for the countless blessings in our own lives. The Sign of the Cross should never be made out of habit or casually. It should always be made with reverence, faith, and a sincere understanding of its meaning.

Varughese P. Issac & Family

Our family moved to Philadelphia from India in 1990. At that time, our family consisted of my wife, Rachel, our daughter Marina, and myself, Varughese. That same year, we joined SGMOC, which was worshipping at the Church of the Savior on 38th and Chestnut Streets. Mathai Achen and the church family welcomed us wholeheartedly and made us feel at home.

I have served as an Acolyte since 1968, having been ordained by the late Thoma Mar Dionysius of Niranam. After joining SGMOC, I continued this ministry and have been blessed with many opportunities to serve the Church, including multiple terms on the Board of Directors, Church Treasurer, Diocesan Assembly Member, and currently as a Malankara Association Member.

Our two younger daughters, Marilyn and Rosilyn, were both baptized at the Chestnut Street church and all three were actively involved in church life through the choir, Youth League, Sunday School, and other activities. My wife, Rachel, has also been a dedicated member of MMVS.

We are deeply grateful to God for the many blessings and opportunities He has given our family to worship, serve, and grow within this church community. As we celebrate 50 years of the Church's presence in Philadelphia, we give thanks for God's guidance and for the intercession of St. Mary, St. Thomas, and St. Gregorios. We pray for continued blessings upon our Church and its members for generations to come.

Jinu John & Family

Golden Jubilee Family Sponsor
Proof copy

When many of us came to the United States of America from Kerala, we brought with us more than dreams and hopes for a better future. We also brought our culture, traditions, memories, and most importantly, the Orthodox faith that was passed down to us by our parents and grandparents. It is the faith we grew up with, the faith that has guided us through different stages of our lives, and the faith we now hope to pass on to our children.

Starting a life in a new country came with many changes and challenges. Through it all, we are grateful that we have been able to continue living and growing in our Malankara Orthodox faith. Through SGMOC, we found more than a church. We found a spiritual home and a community where we could pray together, celebrate together, and support one another. Over the years, this parish has become an important part of our life and our journey here in America.

One of the greatest blessings for us as parents is seeing our children grow up in this same faith. It brings us joy to see them attend Sunday School, participate in Holy Qurbana and church celebrations, and spend time with their church friends. Through these experiences, they are learning about God, our faith, and the traditions that have been part of our families for generations. At the same time, they are building friendships and creating memories that we hope they will carry with them throughout their lives.

As SGMOC celebrates 50 years, we are especially grateful for those who came before us. Their faith, hard work, and sacrifices gave families like ours a place to call our spiritual home. They passed this faith on to us, and now it is our turn to pass it on to our children. Our hope and prayer is that they will carry it with them wherever life takes them and, one day, pass it on to the generations that follow.

We are members of St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church at Bensalem, originally St. Thomas Indian Orthodox Church of Philadelphia since 1976 under the leadership of Late Very Rev. K. Mathai Cor Episcopos.

Our children Ajay and Anju grew up in this church. They were part of the first Youth League and its publication 'REFLECTIONS'. Ajay also served as an altar boy. Mathai Achen's support and guidance helped them to grow up to be the responsible professionals they are now.

Now we are very happy to continue as the members of this church under the guidance and leadership of Rev. Fr. Shibu Venad Mathai who is an asset to St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church.

Jiji Koshy & Family

Golden Jubilee Family Sponsor
Proof copy

Jiji Koshy was born in the early 1960s and raised in Vazhoor, Kottayam, Kerala, as the youngest of eight children. His family was active in St. Peter’s Malankara Syrian Orthodox Church in Pulikkalkavala. After earning a degree in Business and Administration and working as a Logistics Manager in Kerala, Jiji immigrated to the United States in 1991, settling in New Jersey with his eldest brother, George.

Beena Abraham was born in the late 1960s and raised in North Paravur, Ernakulam, the second of three children of Areekal Abraham Tharian and Vazhappilli Sucy Abraham. After earning a master’s degree in physics, Beena married Jiji in 1992. Jiji settled in Philadelphia with his brother Thomas, where he helped establish St. Mary’s Malankara Syrian Orthodox Church; Beena and their daughter Jane joined him in 1996.

In the summer of 2000, a season of change — a new job, a new home, their eldest starting kindergarten and a third child on the way — brought them to St. Gregorios, shortly before Joanne was born. Over the years both became active in the ministries, and their daughters in the Youth League and Sunday School. In 2023 Beena made parish history as the first woman to serve as Treasurer and Trustee.

Jiji grew up serving at the altar in his home parish, and after immigrating faced pressure from colleagues and family to join other denominations. He stayed with the faith handed down to him, and encourages those around him to do the same. Beena set out to be a physicist and found instead a profession in computers; leaving her family in Kerala, she built a new one here, and came to find in SGMOC a second home.

Jiji established and runs Alma Digital Vision, his photography and videography business, and Beena works as an Enterprise Systems Programmer with the City of Philadelphia. Their daughters have gone on to science research, engineering, literature and writing. Above all the family treasures the church community that has carried and enriched their lives.
